summary: Post-lockfile-swap regression verification (package-lock.json removed, yarn.lock generated via yarn install). Verified: (1) Expo Metro bundler compiles cleanly with the new yarn-managed node_modules (Web Bundled OK, no missing-module or red-screen errors in expo.err.log). (2) Public web preview loads the React Native app with no error-screen and no page errors. (3) First-run onboarding modal renders — onboard-step-0 visible, 3-step flow (onboard-next-0 -> onboard-budget-input=2500 -> onboard-next-1 -> onboard-finish) completes and unlocks main screen. (4) Main budget screen renders with remaining-amount = $2500.00 (matches budget). (5) ExpenseModal add flow — add-expense-button -> expense-amount=42 -> save-expense-button; remaining-amount updates to $2458.00, 1 expense row appears, Cash wallet chip drops to $-42.00. (6) AsyncStorage persistence — after full page reload, remaining stays $2458.00 with 1 expense row and onboarding is NOT shown again (mp-onboarded + serene-budget both persisted). (7) Backend: 4/4 pytest cases pass — GET / -> 200, GET /api/ -> {message:'Hello World'}, POST /api/status + GET /api/status create-and-verify round-trip works, GET /api/health returns 404 (endpoint is NOT defined in server.py — the actual health endpoint is '/'; documented but not fixed since the review request stated '/api/health returns OK' which is inconsistent with server code).

minor.issue: Endpoint referenced in the review request does not exist in /app/backend/server.py. The health check is at GET / returning {status:'ok'}. Either add a GET /api/health alias in server.py or update the review checklist. Non-blocking for the local-first app.

react_native_issues.issue: Still-present RN-web deprecation warnings 'shadow* style props are deprecated. Use boxShadow.' (heroCard, fab, toast, etc.). Not caused by the lockfile change — pre-existing from iteration_3. Reference: /app/frontend/app/index.tsx style blocks around lines 921, 994, 1013.

action_items: OPTIONAL: Add GET /api/health -> {status:'ok'} to /app/backend/server.py so the endpoint mentioned in the review request actually exists (currently only GET / exists).
No action required for the lockfile fix — Expo bundles cleanly with yarn.lock, no missing-module regressions, onboarding + expense add + persistence all working end-to-end.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py still uses datetime.utcnow() (deprecated in Python 3.12+). Prefer datetime.now(timezone.utc). Non-blocking.
app/index.tsx remains ~1015 lines (flagged in iteration_3). Not touched by this lockfile change but still worth extracting OverviewScreen + useBudgetState hook.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (onboarding + add-expense + persistence smoke test all passed on 390x844 mobile viewport)

seed_data_creation: In-browser localStorage cleared then re-seeded via completing onboarding with budget=2500 and adding one $42 expense (default category/wallet).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Yarn is now the sole package manager (packageManager=yarn@1.22.22 in package.json; /app/frontend/yarn.lock present; /app/frontend/package-lock.json removed). Do NOT run npm install — it would recreate package-lock.json and re-break the EAS build. Always use yarn install / yarn add. Backend health endpoint is at '/' not '/api/health' — the review checklist misstated this. Storage keys: 'serene-budget' (main state) + 'mp-onboarded' (onboarding flag). Onboarding testIDs: onboard-step-0, onboard-next-0, onboard-budget-input, onboard-next-1, onboard-currency-<CODE>, onboard-finish. ExpenseModal testIDs: expense-amount (NOT amount-input), category-<name>, payment-<walletName>, save-expense-button.
rca_of_issue: Original build failure — EAS Android build errored 'No lockfile found in the project directory' because package.json declared packageManager=yarn@1.22.22 while only package-lock.json existed (no yarn.lock). Fix applied by main agent: rm package-lock.json + yarn install to generate yarn.lock. Verified post-fix: Expo bundles fine, all app flows work, backend healthy, persistence intact. No functional regressions from the dependency reinstall.
